reason: The Egyptian elite (Pharaoh and his officials, representing the ruling class) are portrayed as people compelled by fear and divine power to relinquish the Israelites, their possessions, and their control of the situation. Egypt as a whole is described as being 'plundered' (ויְנַצְּל֖וּ אֶת־ מִצְרָֽיִם), and the Egyptians are moved by fear ('כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ כֻּלָּ֥נוּ מֵתִֽים - 'we are all dead') to hasten the Israelites' departure. While this passage does not feature detailed negative character development of specific elite individuals, it depicts the Egyptian ruling class as powerless before divine authority and as people whose wealth and dominion are taken from them.
